continuity_scope: Character-layer companion to the existing source-entry pass, scoped to BORI’s Critical Edition as a reference structure for the 18-parvan Sanskrit epic. It is not the sole, complete, or normatively superior Mahābhārata across manuscript, regional, vernacular, devotional, performance, or living traditions.

work_or_witnesses.edition: Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, constituted Sanskrit text with critical apparatus, 18 parvans in 19 volumes (1919–1966)
Kisari Mohan Ganguli public-domain English translation, used only for accessible narrative locators; not asserted to reproduce BORI CE chapter numbering or constituted text

coverage_rule: Principal named acting characters across the declared epic scope: Kuru/Pāṇḍava dynastic actors, principal allies and opponents, named divine/rākṣasa agents materially active in core episodes, and named figures needed for dharma, vows, curses, boons, astras, ritual, and war structures. Unnamed collectives, most genealogy-only figures, and non-acting places/artifacts are excluded.
omissions: Most named combatants, attendants, sages, wives, children, and genealogy-only figures
Harivaṃśa, regional recensions, vernacular retellings, performance traditions, and modern adaptations
Passages absent from or differently constituted in the BORI CE
Claims about contemporary Hindu practice or all South Asian social history
uncertainties: BORI CE is a scholarly constituted text from 1,259 manuscripts, not an original autograph or a replacement for other Mahābhārata traditions.
The accessible Ganguli translation is not a translation of the BORI CE; every such locator says so explicitly.
Parvan/section naming and numbering can differ across editions and translations.
Dharma, varṇa, deva/asura/rākṣasa, avatāra, ritual, and astra mapping remain contextual and non-game-like.
evidence_basis: BORI’s official metadata establishes the reference continuity. Individual narrative claims use the accessible Ganguli translation with parva/section locators and explicit non-equivalence warning; a future CE-Sanskrit/critical-translation check is required before source-critical integration.

supports: BORI CE methodology, manuscript count, parvan/volume structure, and constituted-text status.
Identified accessible translation used only for narrative locators.
